description: Stage 1 of the Xin Wang SP3 workflow. Produce cell-homogenised 8-group macroscopic cross sections (Sigma_t, Sigma_s g'->g, nu*Sigma_f, chi, diffusion coeff, group speeds, 6 delayed groups) for the Mk1 PB-FHR regions (fuel pebble, blanket, center/outer reflector, control-rod B4C, SS316, flibe) from ENDF/B-VII.0 via njoy-outram-park-fork. Group structure (Wang Table 3.4, lower bounds MeV): 1.4, 2.5e-2, 4.8e-5, 4.0e-6, 5.0e-7, 1.9e-7, 5.8e-8, 0.0. XS parametrised vs flibe density (linear, Eq 2.25) and log(T_fuel) (linear-log, Eq 2.26) for feedback. Scaffolded in nee_soon xin_wang_sp3_workflow::mgxs. BLOCKED on njoy exposing an MGXS export entry point (see njoy-epic bead). Do NOT implement MGXS inside njoy from here.
title: MGXS generation from njoy: 8-group Mk1 FHR cross sections from ENDF/B-VII.0

description: Stage 2 of the Xin Wang SP3 workflow. Build the Mk1 PB-FHR Monte Carlo model in outram-mc-libs: annular pebble-bed CSG/mesh geometry (center reflector r=35cm, active fuel region, blanket pebble ring 20cm, outer reflector, core barrel/downcomer/vessel per Wang Tables 4.1/4.4/4.8/4.9 + Appendix C), FCC pebble lattice (packing 60%, 3cm pebbles, 4730 TRISO/pebble), and RegularMesh + energy/spatial tallies to generate the 8-group MGXS + power-fraction-by-burnup (Fig 4.7) that feed Stage 1/3. Reference the Serpent full-core model (Fig 4.3). BLOCKED on outram-mc MGXS/mesh-tally work (op-6tz.15 multigroup mode + MGXSLibrary, op-6tz.13 RegularMesh+MeshFilter). Compose outram-mc public API only.
title: Mesh + OpenMC MC model for Mk1: geometry, tallies, MGXS generation via outram-mc

design:
## The problem, measured

`outram-park-backend/CLAUDE.md` is **1,867 lines / 115 KB**, loaded in full at
the start of every agent session in this repo, before any task-specific
context. Across the workspace there are **20 agent-instruction files**
totalling ~280 KB (19 `CLAUDE.md` + 1 `AGENTS.md`).

Structure of the root file: 29 top-level sections, 22 subsections, 17
separate "HARD RULE" markers.

The largest sections:

| lines | section |
|---|---|
| 328 | Dogfood KOPITIAM and KOPI-BEANS (HARD RULE) |
| 187 | Human interface layer (mandatory design principle) |
| 100 | Members |
| 84 | WebAssembly — supported target, with a hard caveat |
| 78 | Android / Termux portability (HARD RULE) |
| 77 | Bookkeeping pass (maintainer command) |
| 76 | File path length: 170-character hard cap (HARD RULE) |
| 75 | Rust design rules (mandatory) |
| 73 | Working-hours guardrail (OPT-IN) |
| 72 | Responsible use & data policy (NUS compliance) |

## Why this is worth fixing

**Every rule competes with every other rule for attention.** With 17 hard
rules in one file, an agent has no way to tell which bind on the task in front
of it. The failure mode is not that a rule is missing — it is that a rule is
present, correct, and skimmed past. The 328-line kopi-beans section is
load-bearing for *some* sessions and irrelevant to most; the same is true of
the WASM, Android, working-hours and NUS-compliance sections.

**Reference material and standing rules are mixed together.** "Members"
(100 lines), the bookkeeping-pass command and the API-doc toolchain notes are
things to consult when relevant. The Rust design rules and scope boundary are
things that bind on every edit. They currently read at the same priority.

**Cost is paid every session, on every task.** 115 KB of preamble is charged
against context whether the session is a one-line doc fix or a full solver
port.

## Suggested direction (not prescriptive)

1. **Split standing rules from reference material.** Keep the file to what
   binds on every task — scope boundary, Rust design rules, build/test,
   branch conventions, issue tracking. Move consult-when-relevant material
   (Members, bookkeeping pass, WASM caveats, working-hours, API-doc
   toolchain) to linked documents under `docs/`.
2. **Push crate-specific rules into crate `CLAUDE.md` files**, which already
   exist for 18 crates and are loaded only when working in that tree.
3. **Audit the 17 hard rules.** Some are genuinely universal; some are
   conditional (working-hours is explicitly opt-in, token accounting is
   opt-in) and should not carry the same marker. A hard rule that is
   sometimes off teaches that hard rules are negotiable.
4. **Reconcile `CLAUDE.md` with `AGENTS.md`** (181 lines) — check what is
   duplicated and which is authoritative where they disagree.
5. **Check the crate files for staleness** against the code they describe,
   the same way the parent file's `bn init` bug note is now historical.

## Related

Filed alongside the maturity gate (bn `op-g7cq`), which added ~65 lines to the
root file — the immediate prompt for this cleanup. Both changes push in
opposite directions, which is the point: the rule needed to be written down,
and the file needed to stop growing without a plan.
title: Clean up CLAUDE.md and the agent instruction files
